h1: LLM and RAG Development for Knowledge-Base Assistants
lead: Crenosoft builds AI assistants that answer questions from your own documents, policies, product data and past work, with links to the sources. Built on large language models and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), they give staff and customers accurate answers in seconds.
facts: Answers grounded in your own documents
Connects SharePoint, Google Drive, Notion and more
answer: RAG, or retrieval-augmented generation, is a technique where an AI system first searches your own documents for the passages relevant to a question, then uses a large language model to write an answer based only on those passages. It makes answers more accurate, current and verifiable than a model working from memory.
body:
Why businesses need knowledge-base AI

The answers your staff need are usually written down somewhere: in a policy manual, a product sheet, a past proposal, a support ticket or a shared drive folder nobody can find. People ask colleagues instead, wait for replies or guess. New staff take months to learn where things live. A knowledge-base assistant turns all of that material into something you can simply ask, and it shows exactly where each answer came from.

How RAG works

  1. Ingest: your documents are collected from sources such as SharePoint, Google Drive, Notion, Confluence, websites and databases.
  2. Prepare: documents are cleaned, split into meaningful sections and indexed with embeddings and keywords.
  3. Retrieve: when someone asks a question, the system finds the most relevant passages, filtered by what that user is allowed to see.
  4. Generate: a large language model writes an answer using only those passages.
  5. Cite: the answer links to its sources, and says clearly when the documents don’t contain the answer.

RAG vs fine-tuning vs a plain chatbot

Plain AI chatbotFine-tuned modelRAG assistant
Uses your informationNoLearned during trainingRetrieved live from your documents
Stays currentNoNeeds retrainingUpdates when documents change
Shows sourcesNoNoYes
Respects permissionsNoDifficultYes, per user
Cost to updateNot applicableHighLow

For most business knowledge problems, RAG is the right starting point. Fine-tuning has a place for specialised styles or formats, and we combine the two when it helps.

Use cases we build

  • Internal policy and procedure assistant for HR, operations and compliance questions.
  • Sales enablement assistant that finds case studies, pricing rules and past proposals.
  • Technical support assistant trained on manuals, specifications and resolved tickets.
  • Customer-facing help assistant on your website or portal. See AI chatbot development.
  • Research assistant across large document sets such as contracts, reports or tenders.

Accuracy you can measure

We don’t ask you to trust a demo. Before launch we build an evaluation set: real questions with correct answers, agreed with your subject experts. Every version of the assistant is scored on whether it finds the right sources, answers correctly and declines when it should. After launch we review a sample of conversations and the questions it couldn’t answer, then improve the content and retrieval.

This follows the testing and monitoring practices in the Australian Government’s Guidance for AI Adoption.

Security and permissions

Knowledge bases often contain confidential material, so security is built in:

  • Users only receive answers from documents they already have permission to open
  • Hosting in Australian cloud regions where the services are available
  • AI provider settings that keep your data out of public model training where available
  • Logging of questions and sources for audit
  • Privacy design aligned with the Privacy Act 1988 and the OAIC’s AI product guidance

Technology

We build with leading models from Anthropic, OpenAI and Google, vector databases and hybrid keyword search, and connectors to your document sources. The assistant can live in Microsoft Teams, Slack, your intranet, your website or a dedicated app. Model choices follow provider guidance such as Anthropic’s documentation and OpenAI’s platform docs.

How a RAG project runs

  1. Free AI audit to scope the knowledge, users and questions.
  2. Content review: we check document quality and fill obvious gaps.
  3. Prototype on a subset of your documents, scored against the evaluation set.
  4. Build and connect sources, permissions and the user interface, usually four to eight weeks.
  5. Launch and improve with monthly accuracy reviews.

RAG assistants are one part of our wider AI development services.

Getting your documents ready

A knowledge-base assistant is only as good as the content behind it. During the content review we look for outdated versions, duplicates, conflicting policies and gaps where common questions have no written answer. We flag these to your subject experts and agree which documents are the source of truth. Many clients find this clean-up valuable in its own right, because staff were already struggling with the same conflicting documents before any AI was involved.

We also set up a simple way for subject experts to update content, so the assistant stays accurate as policies and products change.
faqs: What is the difference between RAG and fine-tuning?

RAG retrieves relevant passages from your documents at question time and answers from them, with sources. Fine-tuning changes the model itself through extra training. RAG is cheaper to update, shows sources and respects permissions, so it suits most business knowledge.
Can a RAG assistant respect who can see which documents?
Yes. We filter retrieval by each user’s existing permissions, so people only get answers drawn from documents they are already allowed to open.
Which document sources can you connect?
Common sources include SharePoint, OneDrive, Google Drive, Notion, Confluence, websites, PDFs and databases. If a system has an API or export, we can usually include it.
How do you stop the assistant making things up?
Answers are generated only from retrieved passages, every answer cites its sources, and the assistant is instructed and tested to say when the documents don’t contain an answer.
